title: Southeast Asia Digital Nomad Visa Comparison
description: Compare digital nomad and remote worker visa options across Southeast Asia. Each country offers different requirements, durations, and benefits for location-independent professionals.
disclaimer: This comparison is compiled from publicly available sources for general reference only. Visa requirements change frequently. Always verify current requirements directly with each country's immigration authority before applying. This is not immigration consulting or legal advice.

data.visaCategory: Multiple-entry tourist visa with workcation permissions
data.extensionRules: Multiple entries permitted within 5-year validity. More than 2 visa runs per year may result in entry denial.
data.financialRequirement: THB 500,000 (~USD 15,340) in savings, or proof of foreign income
data.incomeProof: Bank statements or payslips showing foreign income
data.healthInsurance: Travel insurance typically required for application
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work for foreign companies and freelance for non-Thai clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Thai companies or obtain Thai work permit
data.dependents: Yes — spouses and unmarried children under 20
data.taxImplications: Tax resident if staying >180 days/year. Foreign income taxed only if remitted to Thailand in same calendar year.
data.recentChanges: Launched July 2024. Full e-visa system from January 2025. Visa run enforcement tightened November 2025.

data.visaCategory: Single-entry work visa for remote workers
data.extensionRules: Renewable for additional years. Must apply for renewal before expiry without leaving Indonesia.
data.financialRequirement: USD 60,000 minimum annual income from foreign employer, plus USD 2,000 savings in last 3 months
data.incomeProof: Employment contract with foreign company and bank statements
data.healthInsurance: Not formally required but recommended; private healthcare available
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — must work for foreign employer (mandatory requirement)
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Indonesian companies or accept local employment
data.taxImplications: Foreign-source income generally not taxed. Tax residency rules still evolving for E33G holders.
data.multipleEntry: No — single entry. Must renew for continued stay.
data.recentChanges: Launched 2024. Policy refinements ongoing. Growing acceptance among immigration authorities.

data.extensionRules: Renewable for additional 12 months online without leaving Malaysia. Processing takes 6–8 weeks.
data.incomeProof: Proof of foreign income source and employment/freelance documentation
data.healthInsurance: Not formally required; private healthcare widely available and affordable
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work remotely for foreign employers and freelance for foreign clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Malaysian companies
data.applicationFee: MYR 1,000 (~USD 220) main applicant; MYR 500 (~USD 110) per dependent
data.dependents: Yes — spouse and children can accompany
data.taxImplications: Reduced tax rate on Malaysian-source income for first 182 days. Foreign income not taxed if stay under 60 days.
data.recentChanges: Eligibility expanded 2025 to include non-tech professionals. Income thresholds vary by field.

data.officialName: Philippine Digital Nomad Visa (Executive Order No. 86)
data.maxStay: 12 months, renewable once (24 months maximum total)
data.extensionRules: Renewable for one additional 12-month period in-country. Maximum 2-year total stay.
data.financialRequirement: USD 24,000 minimum annual income from foreign sources
data.incomeProof: Proof of remote employment or freelance contracts with foreign clients
data.healthInsurance: Yes — valid international health insurance required throughout entire stay
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work for foreign employers and freelance for overseas clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Philippines-based companies or clients
data.dependents: No — details not yet confirmed for initial program
data.taxImplications: Tax-free on foreign-source income. DN visa holders not considered Philippine tax residents.
data.multipleEntry: Yes — expected to include multiple-entry privileges
data.recentChanges: Launched June 2025. Still in pilot phase. Procedures being refined based on initial applications.
